## Prolonged treatment

For specified special diseases/illnesses, prolonged treatment requires approval from **Dy. HOD (HR)**. Reimbursement is made at **90%**, subject to that approval. The listed diseases are: tuberculosis; hypertension; diabetes mellitus not controlled by diet therapy; coronary artery disease/disorder; bronchial asthma; epilepsy; hypo- or hyperthyroidism; arthritis; allergy; thalassemia; Parkinson’s disease/multi-system atrophy; autism; neurological disorders; hypercholesterolemia; osteoporosis; primary sclerosing cholangitis; autoimmune hemolytic anemia; glaucoma; and ITP (immune thrombocytopenia). [E2]

Follow-up OPD treatment after IPD treatment for **cancer, AIDS, kidney failure and transplantation, liver failure and transplantation, heart bypass surgery, and other surgical or non-surgical heart interventions** is also reimbursable at **90%**, when taken from the institution where the IPD treatment occurred, a nominated or Government hospital, or a DMRC Medical Consultant. [E2]

### Approval validity

Approval by Dy. HOD (HR) is valid for a maximum of **two years or until completion of treatment, whichever is earlier**, as prescribed by the doctor. If treatment must continue after two years, the employee must obtain fresh approval from Dy. HOD (HR) through **ESS**. For continuity, applying for further treatment before the existing approval expires is advised. [E3]

The reimbursement schedule also lists **ophthalmic and prolonged disease treatment** at **90% reimbursement**. [E1]

The retrieved evidence does not provide a general documentary definition of **“speed”** itself. In the ATP operating manual, the speedometer indicates speed and displays these categories: **current speed, target speed, advisory speed, warning speed, and maximum safety speed (recommended speed)**. The interlocking interface also supports setting speed limits, including **5, 10, 55, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85, 95, 105, and 115 km/h**, and provides a command to release the speed limit. ## PEA resetting

1. After the passenger conversation, select the PEA using the up/down arrow and move it to **“Hold/Park CALL.”** [E1]  
2. At a station, use the **“PAB Override”** soft button on the **Door page of TIMS** if movement must be restored before physical resetting: touch **“PAB OVERRIDE”**, then touch **“OK”** in the confirmation window. This overrides all operated PEAs and energizes ADCR. [E2][E3]  
3. The operated PEA/PAB must then be **physically reset at a convenient location, before changing ends at the terminal station**. [E1][E2][E3]  
4. Physical resetting is required before the PEA can be used again. An overridden PAB remains non-operational until it is physically reset. [E1][E2]

If the PEA is not manually reset before cab change, announcements may not play properly. [E1] After physical resetting, the PEA indication/status should clear; the retrieved evidence states that the PEA light turns off and the ETU indication on the TIMS Door page goes off after resetting. [E1]

## Door isolation procedure — identify the applicable fleet, line, and operating mode first

**Do not treat the following procedures as interchangeable.** Before applying any door-isolation method, identify the train fleet/configuration, the applicable line, and—where relevant—the operating mode. The retrieved documents prescribe distinct methods and conditions for RS-1, RS-13, RS-17, RS-10, RS-3, Airport trains, and the RS-1 8-car D-unit on Line-1. [E1] [E5] [E8] [E12] [E40] [E42]

| Fleet / scenario | Applicable isolation method and key condition |
|---|---|
| **RS-1** | The documented procedure mechanically isolates the defective door using a square key, with TIMS used for fault/status checks and isolation confirmation. [E35] [E38] |
| **RS-13** | Door isolation may be mechanical from inside or outside the saloon, or electrical from TIMS for a normal door that is **closed and locked**. [E1] |
| **RS-13 — outside saloon** | Manual isolation should preferably follow the RS-1 manual procedure; outside-saloon isolation is permitted in exceptional cases. [E37] |
| **RS-1 8-car D-unit, Line-1 only** | Isolation from inside the saloon is prohibited; isolate from outside only. [E5] |
| **RS-17** | Faulty or malfunctioning door(s) shall be isolated strictly mechanically; the documented steps distinguish UTO with TO/RA/ETO and Non-UTO operation. [E40] [E41] |
| **RS-10** | TCMS isolation is available only for an eligible closed door that is faulty/normal and not already isolated; separate mechanical-isolation requirements are also documented. [E42] [E45] |
| **RS-3** | TIMS isolation is possible only when the door is closed and a fault is registered in the corresponding DCU. [E8] |
| **Airport trains** | Mechanical isolation is followed by verification on the TCMS incidence screen. [E12] |

## RS-1: fault assessment and mechanical isolation from inside

For a door that fails to close or open, the Train Operator must first give a valid door open/close command of about **1 second** and check door status on TIMS. A blinking indication means a fault is logged in the DCU; it does **not necessarily** mean that the door is un-operational or that the fault is permanent. On TIMS, yellow background means the door is closed and pink background means it is open. [E35]

1. If the door remains blinking after door closing, observe ADCR and DPR. If both are energized, there is no need to isolate the door. [E38]  
2. If ADCR and DPR are de-energized, attempt two additional door-open then door-close cycles. [E38]  
3. If the fault persists, inform OCC, give a **DOOR OPEN COMMAND**, and follow the Cab Leaving Procedure; the last command must be the Door Open Command. [E38]  
4. Approach the defective door, identified on TIMS, via the platform/outside of the train. Close and lock it from the platform side by pushing one leaf towards the other; the other leaf will move automatically. [E38]  
5. Enter the saloon through a door adjacent to the defective door. Before isolation, slightly separate the door leaves to check whether it is locked. If they open, close the door with sufficient force until it is properly locked. [E38]  
6. Insert the square key through the panel hole and turn it anti-clockwise by approximately **60°**. A click indicates electrical isolation, but the key must be moved beyond **40° from the click sound** to ensure positive locking. [E38]  
7. Confirm locking by physically attempting to separate the leaves. Paste a **“Door Isolation sticker”** on the isolated saloon-door leaf glass so that it is visible and readable from both inside and outside the train. [E38]  
8. Exit through the adjacent saloon door, return to the cab via the platform, and confirm the defective-door isolation and ADCR/DPR status on TIMS. [E38]  

If a door shows **“isolated”** on TIMS without being physically and deliberately isolated, the Train Operator must isolate that door. [E36]

### RS-1 movement condition after isolation

Before movement, verify that all doors are closed/isolated and determine whether ADCR and DPR are energized. Distinguish whether ADCR de-energization is caused by PEA operation or a door failure. If the issue is PEA only, use the PAB override soft key on TIMS for a temporary rectification; PEA resetting can be done at the terminal station. If DPR and ADCR remain de-energized, inform OCC, operate DPLCOS, and move the train under the stated subsequent procedure. [E39]

## RS-13: isolation from outside the saloon

For RS-13, manual isolation should preferably follow the RS-1 manual procedure. In exceptional cases, it may be performed from outside the saloon as follows. [E37]

1. At stations with PSDs, unlock and open the EED using the square key to access the external saloon-door isolation switch. [E37]  
2. Slide the movable PSD door leaf to access the intended door’s isolation switch/ERD. [E37]  
3. Open the isolation-switch flap. [E37]  
4. **After ensuring the defective door is properly closed and locked**, use the square key to rotate the isolation switch to the Isolate position. [E37]  
5. Return the PSD to the open condition. If the door is closed and locked, operate the lever behind the PSD to slide it back. [E37]  
6. Normalize the EED by gently pushing it towards the closed position. [E37]  
7. Confirm the isolated-door status on the TIMS Door page. [E37]  
8. Close all applicable saloon doors and PSDs using a door-close command or the PSD control panel. Confirm all saloon doors and PSDs are closed before departure. [E37]  

For RS-13, a door-isolation switch is provided inside and outside each saloon door. Operate it clockwise with a square key to isolate and anti-clockwise to normalize. A normal saloon door may also be electrically isolated from TIMS only when it is closed and locked. [E1]

### RS-1 8-car D-unit exception — Line-1 only

For the RS-1 8-car D-unit on Line-1, inside-saloon door isolation is currently prohibited. If isolation is required, it must be performed from outside the saloon only. [E5]

## RS-17: mechanical isolation and reset

In RS-17 trains, a door that is faulty or malfunctions for any reason **shall be isolated strictly mechanically**. [E40]

The retrieved RS-17 isolation table documents the following sequence from its locking-check step onward:

1. Before isolating, check that the door is locked by slightly separating the leaves. If they open, close the door with sufficient force so that it is properly locked. This is stated for both UTO mode with TO/RA/ETO and Non-UTO mode. [E41]  
2. Insert the square key on the metallic square head of the lock-out device and rotate it towards the Isolate position. The lock-out device is on the left door leaf when viewed from inside the train; “Reset” denotes normal and “Isolate” denotes isolated. [E41]  
3. Verify isolation by applying force to separate the leaves. [E41]  
4. TO/RA/ETO shall check that the concerned door’s DIL glows steadily. [E41]  
5. Paste the Door Isolation Sticker above PSD height, visible and readable from inside and outside. [E9]  
6. TO/RA/ETO shall inform TC/OCC. TC/OCC shall check available indications and confirm that the door is properly isolated. [E9]  
7. The operator exits through an adjacent saloon door. TC/OCC then gives a door-open command; after the operator reports boarding the departing-side cab, TC/OCC gives a door-close command. The operator checks door status, ADCR status on TCMS, and other available indications. [E9]  

For reset, rotate the lock-out device to Reset using the square key and remove the sticker. In Non-UTO mode, additionally open the coving panel, set the DCU toggle switch to **ON**, and close the panel. RS-17 mechanical isolation/resetting may also be performed from outside. [E9]

## RS-10: electronic isolation through TCMS

1. On the Operation Menu, press **ISOLATION** and select **DOOR** on the Isolation screen. [E16]  
2. Select the required car and select **ISOLATE**. [E16]  
3. A door can be selected only if it is closed and failed and not already isolated; otherwise, only status is shown and selection is invalid. [E16]  
4. Select the required door and press **ENTER** to isolate it. Alternatively, select **ALL DOOR** and **ENTER**; TCMS sends an isolation command to eligible doors in the selected car. [E16]  
5. To reset, select **ISOLATE RESET**, select an isolated door, and press **ENTER**. **ALL DOOR** may be used to reset all isolated doors in the selected car. [E16]  

### RS-10 mechanical isolation — documented extract

The documented mechanical-isolation requirements include using the square key on the lock-out device and rotating it toward the red dot—clockwise from inside the saloon and anti-clockwise from outside. Confirm isolation by trying to separate the leaves, check that DIL glows steadily, and place a Door Isolation Sticker above PSD height. [E15]

After mechanical isolation, RA must inform TC/OCC; TC/OCC confirms isolation from available indications. Subsequent door commands and the RA’s movement toward the departing-side cab are controlled by TC/OCC, followed by a check of door and ADCR status on TCMS and other indications. [E45]

## RS-3: electronic isolation through TIMS

RS-3 TIMS isolation is possible only for a door that is **closed** and has a fault registered in its corresponding DCU. [E8]

1. On the TIMS Door page, press **DOOR ISOLATION**. [E8]  
2. On the Door Isolation screen, select the defective car and press **ISOLATE**. [E8]  
3. In the Select Target Door window, select the defective door and press **ENTER**. A door that is not closed, or a closed door that is not faulty, cannot be selected. [E8]  

## Airport trains: mechanical isolation, reset, and movement

For a persistent door fault, first give a valid door open/close command of about **1 second** and check TCMS. A blinking status only shows a DCU fault logged and does not necessarily establish a permanent or un-operational door condition. If status remains unknown, attempt two additional open/close cycles; if the fault persists, inform OCC and isolate the door. [E48]

The retrieved mechanical-isolation sequence is:

1. Leave the cab under the Cab Leaving Procedure and proceed to the faulty door. [E12]  
2. Open the roof-top panel and switch off Service Toggle Switch **S6**. [E12]  
3. Use the clutch at the top-left of the assembly to try to separate the leaves—even if the door is physically closed—then close them manually with sufficient force. [E12]  
4. Pull the door lock switch/isolation bolt outwards and rotate it to the right to mechanically isolate the door. Verify locking by attempting to separate the leaves manually. [E12]  
5. Paste the Door Isolation Sticker where it is visible and readable from both inside and outside. [E12]  
6. Return to the cab, verify on the TCMS incidence screen that the door is blue, continue in service, and inform OCC. [E12]  

To reset, open the roof-top panel, pull the isolation bolt outward and rotate it left to unlock, then remove the Door Isolation Sticker. [E12]

For movement after isolation, all doors must be closed/isolated. If the traction loop shows green, move under the applicable procedure. If it remains red, set the **Door Loop bypass Switch** to ON and move under the applicable procedure. If the door loop remains not OK—red **DOORS OPEN** on the LOOPS screen—the Train Operator shall operate the door-loop bypass switch after informing OCC. [E12]

## Limitation of the retrieved evidence

The retrieved evidence establishes several fleet-specific procedures but does **not** establish which procedure governs for an unspecified train, line, configuration, or operating mode. The RS-17 isolation table is retrieved only from its locking-check step onward, and the RS-10 mechanical-isolation extract begins after earlier mechanical steps. Therefore, the RS-17 and RS-10 mechanical sequences above are limited to the steps explicitly evidenced here. [E41] [E45]

## High-wind procedure — Line 8 (BCGN–JPW section)

The retrieved procedure is specifically for **Line 8** and covers elevated-station platform-track segments within the wind sensor’s jurisdiction. It does not establish a complete procedure for every line or every high-wind operating scope. [E1][E17]

### 1. Wind speed reaches 70 km/h but remains below 90 km/h

1. The ATS Central Server forwards the wind-system message to all Traffic Controller (TC) ATS MMIs. A **“TSR and Platform Hold application”** dialog and corresponding alarms/events are generated. [E1]
2. The TC/OCC shall immediately acknowledge the pop-up. This automatically applies a **45 km/h TSR** to elevated platform-area track segments and a **Platform Hold** at station platforms in the affected wind-sensor jurisdiction. If a more restrictive TSR of **less than 45 km/h** is already in force, it shall not be updated. [E1]
3. The TC shall inform the CHC/ACC of the measures taken. The CHC/ACC shall consult the ASC to verify the ATS–wind-sensor interface input. [E17]
4. In consultation with the ACC/CHC, the TC shall instruct available RAs to board trains as required. After all available RAs have boarded, the TC shall manually remove the Platform Hold to allow trains to proceed. [E17]
5. RA/ETO personnel shall proceed with **extreme caution** and closely monitor OHE condition and potential infringement of the Structure/Offset Distance (SOD) until all sections are confirmed safe. If an abnormality occurs, the RA/ETO shall stop the train immediately and inform the TC/OCC. Once all sections are verified safe, the ETO shall be withdrawn from the trains. [E3]
6. The ACC/CHC shall instruct the IC to make announcements inside trains to keep passengers informed. The Traction Power Controller (TPC) and Civil Controller shall monitor the OHE and track, respectively, using CCTV feeds from cameras installed at the front of the train. [E4]
7. Station Controllers not assigned to ETO duties may be used to monitor platform areas and tracks by line of sight. [E4]

### 2. Wind speed reaches or exceeds 90 km/h

1. The TC shall immediately acknowledge the ATS pop-up. This automatically applies a **20 km/h TSR** to elevated platform-area track segments and a **Platform Hold** at station platforms within the wind-sensor jurisdiction. An already-active TSR of **less than 20 km/h** shall not be updated. [E17]
2. The TC shall inform the CHC/ACC, and the CHC/ACC shall consult the ASC to verify the ATS–wind-sensor interface input. [E17]
3. Trains already running shall reach the next platform NSP and **shall not move until the wind speed drops below 85 km/h and remains below 85 km/h for 5 minutes**. [E17]
4. The retrieved extract does not show the remaining operational actions for this ≥90 km/h case, such as the full boarding, monitoring, passenger-information, and restoration sequence. Those actions should therefore not be assumed from the available extract. [E17]

### 3. Wind falls after a ≥90 km/h event

When wind speed is **70–85 km/h for 5 minutes** after having reached or exceeded 90 km/h, the ATS MMI gives a non-acknowledgement pop-up recommending manual removal of the TSR from the affected elevated platform-area track segments. [E17]

The available continuation states that the TC shall inform the CHC/ACC and, with prior permission, manually revise the high-wind TSR to **45 km/h** in accordance with the procedure in force. Where the prevailing TSR for a section is below 45 km/h, it shall instead be revised to that prevailing value. The CHC/ACC shall consult the ASC to verify the ATS–wind-sensor interface input. [E2]

Before revising to the prevailing value or 45 km/h, the TC shall first remove the 20 km/h TSR. During manual revision at a station’s platform-area track segment, the TC shall apply a train hold at the preceding station platform to prevent a train exceeding 45 km/h during platform entry. [E2]

The E2 extract is truncated; therefore, any further actions or the complete sequence for this 70–85 km/h case cannot be verified from the retrieved evidence. [E2]

### 4. Normalisation after wind falls below 70 km/h

When wind speed is **below 70 km/h for 5 minutes**, the ATS MMI recommends manual removal of the high-wind TSR. The TC shall inform the CHC and, with the CHC’s prior permission, manually revise or remove the TSR. The CHC/ACC shall verify the ATS–wind-sensor interface input with the ASC. [E3]

The high-wind TSR shall be removed except where a prevailing TSR exists; in that case, the TC shall revise it to the prevailing value. Once all sections are confirmed safe, the RA/ETO shall be withdrawn from the trains. [E3]

The evidence refers to following Para 5.2 for **“Normalization of Train Services,”** but that paragraph is not included in the retrieved material; therefore, the complete restoration sequence cannot be stated. [E3]

### 5. Interface failure or multiple wind triggers

- If the ATS–wind-sensor interface is found malfunctioning after consultation with ASC/OCC/MB-2, SGC and ASC shall be informed for corrective action. The evidence directs staff to follow **Para 9.1** for train manning and speed restrictions in the JPW–BCGN section. [E4]
- If the ATS–wind-sensor interface fails or is unavailable, **Para 9.1 shall be followed**. The contents of Para 9.1 are not included in the retrieved evidence. [E4]
- Station Controllers who are not assigned ETO duties may be used for line-of-sight monitoring of platform areas and tracks. [E4]
- If multiple TSR pop-up triggers are received before the first dialog is closed, the dialog shall be updated using the **most restrictive recommended TSR value**. [E4]

### Scope limitation

The documented high-wind procedure retrieved here is for **Line 8 (BCGN–JPW)**. The evidence also contains general TSR-control provisions for Lines 1–4, including manual/caution-order fallback where system imposition is unavailable, but it does not explicitly link those provisions to the Line-8 high-wind procedure. [E19][E20][E24][E25] Therefore, they should not be treated as a confirmed Line-8 high-wind substitute without the applicable authority or cross-reference.

- **Wrong driving mode — code 180 274:** Brake to standstill, move the Master Control Handle to coast, select Forward or ATP driving mode, then try to activate Coupling Speed mode again. [E5]

The supplied excerpts do **not establish** which high-wind procedure or wind-speed threshold applies to the reported condition of “wind speed 65,” including its unit, location, direction, or required train-operating response. They therefore do not show that a wind reading of 65 triggers a 65 km/h TSR—or any particular TSR, operating mode, or movement instruction. [E21][E23][E25]

For the **L-7 Extension Section (MKPR–MUPR)**, any TSR must apply to a particular track section and direction, must be below the Permanent Speed Restriction for that section/direction, and must have an ATS entry equal to the operational-speed limit. [E21]

## If a 65 km/h TSR has actually been imposed for the L-7 Extension Section (MKPR–MUPR)

The following ATS/ATP values apply only to an imposed TSR of **65 km/h** in the L-7 Extension Section procedure:

| Imposed TSR | Target speed shown to TO on MMI/DMI ATP | ATO running speed | Emergency-braking speed |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 65 km/h | 60 km/h | 62 km/h | 65 km/h |

[E23]

These are TSR-system values. The supplied excerpts do not establish that wind speed 65 is a condition for imposing this TSR. [E23]

## Controls applicable after a TSR is imposed for the L-7 Extension Section (MKPR–MUPR)

1. The Traffic Controller is to advise Crew Control and the Station Controllers adjacent to the TSR section about TSRs to be enforced, maintain a record, and arrange notice-board/sign-on information for RA/ETO personnel. [E22]  
2. Where special precautions are necessary, a caution order must state the affected kilometres, reason, and travel speed. [E32]  
3. The TSR speed-table provisions apply when brakes on all bogies are working normally. If any bogie brakes are isolated or faulty, follow MRGR-2020 clause 30(9) and other relevant instructions. [E25]

For the L-7 Extension Section procedure, when a TSR below 30 km/h is imposed in UTO mode:

1. The Traffic Controller informs RSC. [E25]  
2. UTO operation is suspended in the affected section. [E25]  
3. Crew Control and OCC ensure availability of RA and ETO, respectively, for movement through that section. [E25]  
4. Each passing non-UTO train’s RA/ETO receives a caution order at the station preceding the affected section. [E25]  

For a neutral section in UTO mode, the procedure advises imposing a TSR of 30 km/h or above to avoid manual intervention for remote pantograph-management/VCB open/close. [E25]

- the affected track section or direction; or

## Immediate action

If a station fire alarm operates or smoke/fire is reported, the **Station Controller shall first inform the Traffic Controller and verify by CCTV or actual inspection whether the alarm is genuine.** [E4]

If smoke or fire is present, the Station Controller shall:

1. Inform the Traffic Controller.  
2. Arrange evacuation of passengers **from the area concerned**.  
3. Prevent further access to that area.  
4. If necessary, completely evacuate the station.  
5. Request the Traffic Controller to arrange for trains not to stop at the station. [E4]

The Traffic Controller shall inform the chief controller, who shall arrange fire-fighting services and, if necessary, ambulance services. [E4]

## Applicability to a concourse-level fire in an underground station

At **Shivaji Stadium (SJSU)**, identified as an underground station, the public areas at concourse, platform, mezzanine, and ground levels are divided into individual fire zones. [E15] The concourse-level fire-zone chart explicitly identifies Zones **20–22** as concourse AHU-room zones and Zones **26–28** as concourse zones, including the SER and S/UPS Room. Zones 23–25 are mezzanine-level zones. [E18]

Accordingly, a verified fire in one of the identified concourse-level zones is a fire in a defined concourse fire zone at this underground station. [E15] [E18]

## Important procedure limitation

The governing procedure provides the above **general station-fire** response when a station fire alarm operates or smoke/fire is reported in a station. [E4] It does **not expressly link** that action sequence to a fire specifically classified as a concourse-level fire zone. Therefore, the evidence supports using the general station-fire procedure—verification, evacuation of the area concerned, prevention of further access, escalation through Traffic Control, and possible whole-station evacuation—but does not establish a separate concourse-specific mandatory action sequence. [E4]

## Evacuation access and smoke-control context

For SJSU, a dynamic smoke-control system is provided. Fixed smoke barriers define each smoke reservoir and are intended to prevent smoke spreading between reservoirs; each zone has a smoke-extraction fan system with motorized smoke and fire dampers. [E15]

Emergency-exit and firemen-staircase doors are normally electromagnetically locked and controlled through the Station Control Room (SCR). In a fire/emergency, pressing the evacuation switch electromagnetically releases all doors so they can be opened physically. [E16] [E17] Emergency exits and firemen staircases at underground stations are provided for commuter emergency access and for firemen’s entry during fires. [E23]

However, the available evidence does **not** specify a concourse-fire smoke-extraction or damper operating mode, identify who must operate the smoke-control system, or prescribe a separate concourse-specific evacuation route. [E15]
